@@ -79,6 +79,7 @@
 		</member>
 		<member name="lower_fade" type="float" setter="set_lower_fade" getter="get_lower_fade" default="0.3">
 			Sets the curve over which the decal will fade as the surface gets further from the center of the [AABB]. Only positive values are valid (negative values will be clamped to [code]0.0[/code]). See also [member upper_fade].
+			[b]Note:[/b] Decal nodes created in the editor default [member lower_fade] to [code]0.0[/code], so that the decal does not fade regardless of the distance between the decal and the surface being affected. This does not apply to Decal nodes created via code, which still default [member lower_fade] to [code]0.3[/code].
body:
I'm going to go ham at this one and explain why.

- Weird way to use "default" as a verb targeting `[member lower_fade]`
	- It's not really "default" in the same sense as what "default" is for properties, either. Let's not get confusing.
- It's weird, and has always been weird, to mention the property itself in its own description, in my opinion.
- Incongruency between singular and plural in the same sentence ("Decal nodes [...]", "so that the decal [...]")
- "so that the decal does not fade [...]" is something that one would ideally **not** describe in this note, but rather in the above description itself, to give the user an idea of what `0.0` does.
	- As is worded currently, it sounds like a justification. But you do not need to justify yourself to the reader, they just need to know it's happening and it's intentional!
- Mentioning what a property "defaults to" is redundant information.
	- It's in the header of every property's description.
	- As described above, by not even using "default" to describe the editor changing a property's default value, there's no ambiguity.
```suggestion
			[b]Note:[/b] Decal nodes created in the editor initially set this property to [code]0.0[/code]. This does not apply to Decal nodes created via code.
```

If you accept this suggestion, please try to "apply it" to the others descriptions, as well.
